S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: a borehole drilled for the purpose of injecting a secondary substance, for example water, into the pore spaces in a reservoir rock to encourage oil or gas to flow into adjacent producing wells. (An A-Z of Offshore Oil & Gas by Harry Whitehead, 2nd Ed, 1983, Gulf Publishing Company)

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unspecified
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The status of the object is unspecified.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dormant
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Temporarily quiet, inactive, not being used.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Proposed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A feature that is proposed between parties.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Abandoned
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Completely deserted; given up.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Zone
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Area of overlap of the unilateral fishing zones of two or more countries

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Indeterminate
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area of the sea of indeterminate jurisdiction where no agreed boundary exist.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multilateral
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Involving two or more states as parties to an agreement.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Ferry
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the manoeuvrability of the ferry vessel, not the various types of ferry vessel.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Free Moving Ferry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A ferry which may have routes that vary with weather, tide and traffic.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cable Ferry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A ferry that follows a fixed route guided by a cable.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Ferry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A winter-time ferry which crosses a lead.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: High Speed Ferry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A high speed water vessel for civilian use.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Factor
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The value of the maximum variation in the vertical clearance of an overhead cable due to an accumulation of ice.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Quality of Vertical Measurement
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The reliability of the value of a sounding.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Depth Known
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth from the chart datum to the seabed (or to the top of a drying feature) is known.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Depth or Least Depth Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth from chart datum to the seabed, or the shoalest depth of the feature is unknown.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Doubtful Sounding
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A depth that may be less than indicated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unreliable Sounding
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A depth that is considered to be an unreliable value.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Least Depth Known
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The shoalest depth over a feature is of known value.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Least Depth Unknown, Safe Clearance at Value Shown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The least depth over a feature is unknown, but there is considered to be safe clearance at this depth.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Value Reported (Not Surveyed)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Depth value obtained from a report, but not fully surveyed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Value Reported (Not Confirmed)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Depth value obtained from a report, which it has not been possible to confirm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Maintained Depth
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth at which a channel is kept by human influence, usually by dredging.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Not Regularly Maintained
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Depths may be altered by human influence, but will not be routinely maintained.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Display Scale
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The value considered by the Data Producer to be the maximum (largest) scale at which the data is to be displayed before it can be considered to be “grossly overscaled”.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Coverage
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicator as to area of data coverage.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coverage Available
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Continuous coverage of spatial objects is available within this area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Coverage Available
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area containing no spatial objects.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 3rd Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the third partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Last Source
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the source which subsequently confirmed the object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Naval Vessel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A vessel operated by a recognized National Naval Authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Survey Boat
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A boat used for hydrographic surveys.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Merchant Ship
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported by a vessel operated by a merchant marine organisation, engaged in the transport of goods for payment.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fishing Vessel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A vessel that is used and equipped for the fishing of living aquatic resources.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Research Vessel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported by a vessel engaged in the business of conducting research into the sea and its environs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Yacht
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported by a yacht, being a privately owned sailing or power boat used for pleasure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Diver
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A person skilled in the practice of diving.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Hydrographic Authority Charts
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information given on a chart published by a recognised Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Hydrographic Authority Notices to Mariners
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information given in a Notice to Mariners published by a recognised Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Hydrographic Authority Radio Navigational Warning
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information given in a Radio Navigational Warning issued by a recognised Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Hydrographic Authority Files
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information held in a files maintained by a recognized Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Hydrographic Authority Wreck Information
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information held in wreck records maintained by a recognised Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lloyds and Marine Underwriters Reports
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from reports published by Lloyds or another marine underwriter.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Owner
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: One who has the legal or rightful title to something.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coast Guard
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Organization keeping watch on shipping and coastal waters according to governmental law; normally the authority with responsibility for search and rescue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hydrographic Note Report or Ship Visit
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information provided by a third party as a result of receipt of a ship visit or hydrographic note report by a recognised Hydrographic Office or national authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aerial Photography
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The art, science, or process of taking aerial photographs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Geodetic Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey in which the figure and size of the earth is considered. It is applicable for large areas and long lines and is used for the precise location of basic points suitable for controlling other surveys.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Published World War 1 losses
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information published in books or lists of vessels sunk during world war one.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Published World War 2 losses
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was sourced from information published in books or lists of vessels sunk during world war two.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Published other losses
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object was sourced from information published in books or lists of vessels sunk during periods outside of world wars one and two.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Satellite Imagery
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth was determined by using instruments placed aboard an artificial satellite.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Tidal Stream
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the alternating horizontal movement of water associated with the rise and fall of the tide caused by tide producing forces.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flood Stream
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The horizontal movement of water associated with the rising tide. Flood streams generally set towards the shore, or in the direction of the tide progression.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ebb Stream
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The horizontal movement of water associated with falling tide. Ebb streams generally set seaward, or in the opposite direction to the tide progression.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Other Tidal Flow
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any other horizontal movement of water associated with tides, for example rotary flow.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Water Level Effect
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The effect of the surrounding water on an object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Partly Submerged at High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Partially covered and partially dry at high water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Always Dry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Not covered at high water under average meteorological conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Always Under Water/Submerged
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Remains covered by water at all times under average meteorological conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Covers and Uncovers
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Expression intended to indicate an area of a reef or other projection from the bottom of a body of water which periodically extends above and is submerged below the surface. Also referred to as dries or uncovers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Awash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Flush with, or washed by the waves at low water under average meteorological conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Subject to Inundation or Flooding
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area periodically covered by flood water, excluding tidal waters.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Floating
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Resting or moving on the surface of a liquid without sinking.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Bearing
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The horizontal direction of one terrestrial point from another, expressed as the angular distance from a reference direction. It is usually measured from 0 at the reference direction clockwise through 360. The terms bearing and azimuth are sometimes used interchangeably, but in navigation the former customarily applies to terrestrial objects and the latter to the direction of a point on the celestial sphere from a point on the earth. A bearing is designated as true, magnetic, or compass as the reference direction is true, magnetic, or compass north.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Number of Ice Objects
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Defines the number of ice objects (cracks, leads, fractures, icebergs).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Migration Direction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Direction of movement of feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Iceberg Size
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Categorizes the size of an iceberg.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Growler (1 m ASL)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A smaller piece of ice of land origin than a bergy bit and extending no more than 1 metre above sea level. The color is usually white, but sometimes transparent or blue-green or nearly black, normally occupying an area of about 20 square metres. Growlers are distinguished with difficulty when they are surrounded by ice and also in heavy swell.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bergy Bit (1-5 m ASL; 5-15 m Length)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Bergy Bit (1-5 m asl; 5-15 m length).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Iceberg (5-15 m ASL; 15-60 m Length)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A massive piece of ice of varying shape, protruding from 5 to 15 metres above sea level and 15 to 60 metres in length, which has broken away from a glacier or an ice shelf, and which may be afloat or aground. Icebergs by their external look may be subdivided into tabular, dome-shaped, sloping and rounded bergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Iceberg (16 to 45 m ASL; 61 to 120 m Length)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A massive piece of ice of varying shape, protruding from 16 to 45 metres above sea level and 61 to 120 metres in length, which has broken away from a glacier or an ice shelf, and which may be afloat or aground. Icebergs by their external look may be subdivided into tabular, dome-shaped, sloping and rounded bergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Large Iceberg (46 to 75 m ASL; 121 to 200 m Length)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A massive piece of ice of varying shape, protruding from 46 to 75 metres above sea level and 121 to 200 metres in length, which has broken away from a glacier or an ice shelf, and which may be afloat or aground. Icebergs by their external look may be subdivided into tabular, dome-shaped, sloping and rounded bergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Large Iceberg (75 m ASL; 200 m Length)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A massive piece of ice of varying shape, protruding from over 75 metres above sea level and over 200 metres in length, which has broken away from a glacier or an ice shelf, and which may be afloat or aground. Icebergs by their external look may be subdivided into tabular, dome-shaped, sloping and rounded bergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Island Fragment
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large piece of floating ice protruding about 5 m above sea-level, which has broken away from an Arctic ice shelf, having a thickness of 15-30 metres and an area of from a few thousand square meters to 500 square km or more, and usually characterized by a regularly undulating surface which gives it a ribbed appearance from the air.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Island (in the Northern Hemisphere) or Very Large Tabular Berg (in the Southern Ocean)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large piece of floating ice protruding about 5 metres above sea-level, which has broken away from an Arctic ice shelf, having a thickness of 15-30 metres and an area of from a few thousand square metres to 500 square km or more, and usually characterized by a regularly undulating surface which gives it a ribbed appearance from the air.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Radar Target
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An object which reflects a sufficient amount of a radar signal to produce an echo signal on the radar screen.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Bearing
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector bearing specifies the limit of the sector.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Light Characteristic
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The distinct character, such as fixed, flashing, or occulting, which is given to each light to avoid confusion with neighbouring ones.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fixed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A signal light that shows continuously, in any given direction, with constant luminous intensity and colour.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which the total duration of light in a period is clearly shorter than the total duration of darkness and all the appearances of light are of equal duration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Long-Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A single-flashing light in which an appearance of light of not less than two seconds duration is regularly repeated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Quick-Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which flashes are repeated at a rate of not less than 50 flashes per minutes but less than 80 flashes per minutes. It may be: - Continuous quick-flashing: A quick-flashing light in which a flash is regularly repeated. - Group quick-flashing: A quick-flashing light in which a group of two or more flashes, which are specified in number, is regularly repeated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Quick-Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which flashes are repeated at a rate of not less than 80 flashes per minute but less than 160 flashes per minute. It may be:- Continuous very quick-flashing: A very quick-flashing light in which a flash is regularly repeated.- Group very quick-flashing: A very quick-flashing light in which a group of two or more flashes, which are specified in number, is regularly repeated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Continuous Ultra Quick-Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which flashes are regularly repeated at a rate of not less than 160 flashes per minute.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Isophased
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light with all durations of light and darkness equal.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Occulting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which the total duration of light in a period is clearly longer than the total duration of darkness and all the eclipses are of equal duration. It may be: - Single-occulting: An occulting light in which an eclipse is regularly repeated. - Group-occulting: An occulting light in which a group of two or more eclipses, which are specified in number, is regularly repeated. - Composite group-occulting: An occulting light in which a sequence of groups of one or more eclipses, which are specified in number, is regularly repeated, and the groups comprise different numbers of eclipses.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Interrupted Ultra Quick-Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light in which the ultra quick flashes (160 or more per minute) are interrupted at regular intervals by eclipses of long duration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Morse
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which appearances of light of two clearly different durations are grouped to represent a character or characters in the Morse code.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fixed and Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a fixed light is combined with a flashing light of higher luminous intensity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flash and Long-Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a flashing light is combined with a long-flashing light of higher luminous intensity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Occulting and Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which an occulting light is combined with a flashing light of higher luminous intensity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fixed and Long-Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a fixed light is combined with a long-flashing light of higher luminous intensity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Occulting Alternating
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An alternating light in which the total duration of light in each period is clearly longer than the total duration of darkness and in which the intervals of darkness (occultations) are all of equal duration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Long-Flash Alternating
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An alternating single-flashing light in which an appearance of light of not less than two seconds duration is regularly repeated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flash Alternating
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An alternating rhythmic light in which the total duration of light in a period is clearly shorter than the total duration of darkness and all the appearances of light are of equal duration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Quick-Flash Plus Long-Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a group of quick flashes is followed by one or more long flashes in a regularly repeated sequence with a regular periodicity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Quick-Flash Plus Long-Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a group of very quick flashes is followed by one or more long flashes in a regularly repeated sequence with a regular periodicity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ultra Quick-Flash Plus Long-Flash
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a group of ultra quick flashes is followed by one or more long flashes in a regularly repeated sequence with a regular periodicity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Alternating
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A signal light that shows continuously, in any given direction, two or more colours in a regularly repeated sequence with a regular periodicity.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fixed and Alternating Flashing
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhythmic light in which a fixed light is combined with a flashing light of higher luminous intensity and different colour.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Diving Activity
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Type of diving activity taking place.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Commercial Diving
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Diving taking place for financial gain.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sports Diving
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Diving for recreational purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dive Training
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Practical instruction in diving techniques.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minimum Safe Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The minimum safe depth (MSD) applicable to a submarine of a specified height proceeding at a given rate of knots that should normally be used for planning purposes.

S100FC:uom.S100Base:name: foot
S100FC:uom.S100Base:definition: a unit of length equal to 12 inches, 1/6 of a fathom, or 30.480 centimetres

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Name Usage
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the type and display level of the name of a feature in an end-user system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Default Name Display
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The name is intended to be displayed when the end-user system is set to the default name/text display setting.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Alternate Name Display
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The name is intended to be displayed when the end-user system is set to an alternate name/text display setting, for example an alternate language.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Speed Limit
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The maximum allowed rate of travel in an area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Rescue Station
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of aid station based on life saving equipment.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rescue Station with Lifeboat
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where equipment for saving life at sea is maintained; the type of lifeboat may vary from fast, long distance boats to inflatable inshore boats.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rescue Station with Rocket
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A life saving station equipped with line-carrying rocket apparatus.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Refuge for Shipwrecked Mariners
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Shelter or protection from danger or distress at sea.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Refuge for Intertidal Area Walkers
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Shelter or protection from danger in areas exposed to extreme and sudden tides or tidal streams.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lifeboat Lying at a Mooring
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where a lifeboat is moored ready for use.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aid Radio Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A radio station reserved for emergency situations; might also be a public telephone.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Aid Equipment
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where first aid equipment is available.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Restricted Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The official legal status of each kind of restricted area defines the kind of restriction(s), for example the restriction for a 'game reserve' may be 'entering prohibited'.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Offshore Safety Zone
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The area around an offshore installation within which vessels are prohibited from entering without permission. Special regulations protect installations within a safety zone and vessels of all nationalities are required to respect the zone.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nature Reserve
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tract of land or water managed so as to preserve its flora, fauna, physical features, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bird Sanctuary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where birds are bred and protected.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Game Reserve
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where wild animals or birds hunted for sport or food are kept undisturbed for private use.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Seal Sanctuary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where seals are protected.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Degaussing Range
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area, usually about two cables diameter, within which ships' magnetic fields may be measured; sensing instruments and cables are installed on the seabed in the range and there are cables leading from the range to a control position ashore.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Military Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area controlled by the military in which restrictions may apply.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Historic Wreck Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area around certain wrecks of historical importance to protect the wrecks from unauthorized interference by diving, salvage or deposition (including anchoring).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Navigational Aid Safety Zone
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area around a navigational aid which vessels are prohibited from entering.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Minefield
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area laid and maintained with explosive mines for defence or practice purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Swimming Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which people may swim and therefore vessel movement may be restricted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Waiting Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area reserved for vessels waiting to enter a harbour.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Research Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area where marine research takes place.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dredging Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area where dredging is taking place.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish Sanctuary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where fish (including shellfish and crustaceans) are protected.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ecological Reserve
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tract of land or water managed so as to preserve the relation of plants and living creatures to each other and to their surroundings.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Wake Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which a vessels' speed must be reduced in order to reduce the size of the wake it produces.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Swinging Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area where vessels turn.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Environmentally Sensitive Sea Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A generic term which may be used to describe a wide range of areas, considered sensitive for a variety of environmental reasons.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Particularly Sensitive Sea Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area that needs special protection through action by IMO because of its significance for regional ecological, socio-economic or scientific reasons and because it may be vulnerable to damage by international shipping activities.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Disengagement Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area near a fairway where vessels can go to clear the way or make an about turn and possibly return to a waiting area when nautical conditions impose it.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Port Security Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which defence, law and treaty enforcement, and counter-terrorism activities that fall within the port and maritime domain apply.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coral Sanctuary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place where coral is protected.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Recreation Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which recreational activities regularly take place and therefore vessel movement may be restricted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Maritime Notification Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which notification is required between respective military authorities of future military exercises/activities.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Last Sensor
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates by the use of which sensor the object was subsequently confirmed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Acoustic Sensor
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported as a result of a sound signal being returned from the SBO.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Magnetic Sensor
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object was reported as a result of detecting a fluctuation in the local magnetic field.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Video Sensor
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported as a result of a sighting through electronic visual equipment.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Found by Diver
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth was determined by a person skilled in the practice of diving.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Physical Snag
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported as a result of the object fouling lines, anchors or fishing nets.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Observed Sinking
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported as a result of a first hand observation of the object sinking.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Reported Sinking
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object was reported as a result of a report made by a third party or from published information.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: None Reported
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The method by which the object was found was not reported.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Level Ice
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has not been affected by deformation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Level (Undeformed)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Has not been affected by deformation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Deformed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice in which one piece has overridden another.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Concentration of Hills
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes the degree of hilling in and ice area (usually multiyear ice).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Few Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Few hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight Concentration of Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Slight concentration of hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight to Moderate Concentration of Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Slight to moderate concentration of hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Concentration of Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Moderate concentration of hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate to Heavy Concentration of Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Moderate to heavy concentration of hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Heavy Concentration of Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Heavy concentration of hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Hills
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No hills.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Geodesic Line Type
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The shortest line on the spheroid joining two points.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Frequency Shore Station Receives
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The shore station receiver frequency.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Vessels Characteristics Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The value of a particular characteristic such as a dimension or tonnage of a vessel.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Radar Station
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of radar station based on the services offered.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Radar Surveillance Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A radar station established for traffic surveillance.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coast Radar Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A shore-based station which the mariner can contact by radio to obtain a position.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Tidal Range
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The average difference in height between high and low tides.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Signal Period
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The time occupied by an entire cycle of intervals of light and eclipse.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Interoperability Identifier
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A common unique identifier for entities which describe a single real-world feature, and which is used to identify instances of the feature in end-user systems where the feature may be included in multiple data product types.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Boundary Line
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the category of a boundary .

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Administrative Boundary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A line of demarcation between controlled areas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: De Facto Boundary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An existing line of separation not officially recognized by various governments.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: International Maritime Boundary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The boundary at sea between two coastal States as established by International Law.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Median Line
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A line every point of which is equidistant from the nearest points on the baselines of two or more states between which it lies.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Frequency Shore Station Transmits
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The shore station transmitter frequency.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Runway Length
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The total length of the longest runway.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Scale Value Maximum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The largest scale for the range of survey scale.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Fishing Facility
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of fishing facility provided based on different fishing methods.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fishing Stake
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Poles or stakes placed in shallow water to outline a fishing ground or to catch fish.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish Trap
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure (usually portable) for catching fish.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish Weir
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A fence of stakes or stones set in a river or along the shore to trap fish.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Tunny Net
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A net built at sea for catching tunny.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Access Restriction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A restriction on the right of access.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Originator
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The initiator of a project or process.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Clearance Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The vertical clearance measured from the horizontal plane towards the feature overhead.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Jurisdiction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The jurisdiction applicable to an administrative area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: International
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Involving more than one country; covering more than one national area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area administered or controlled by a single nation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: National Sub-Division
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area smaller than the nation in which it lies.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 1st Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in and ice area. Up to three (stage of development/form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Survey Authority
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The authority which was responsible for the survey.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Ice Thickness
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Specifies the maximum thickness of ice in centimetres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category Of Seagrass
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The type or family of seagrass depicted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cymodoceaceae
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A small family of tropical submerged marine plants (order Naiadales) with slender linear leaves and tiny greenish flowers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hydrocharitaceae
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A family of very simple widely distributed nearly stemless aquatic herbs (order Naiadales) with a 6-parted perianth and somewhat fleshy fruit.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Posidoniaceae
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The monogeneric family Posidoniaceae encompasses P. oceanica and another eight species living off the coasts of Southern Australia.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zosteraceae
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A family of widely distributed marine or aquatic herbs (order Naiadales) that is nearly or exactly equivalent to Potamogetonaceae.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Value of Sounding
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The value of the measurement of a sounding relative to the chart datum.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Contamination
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes the degree of contamination (aretial coverage) in thirds based on the Russian 3-point scale.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No or Insignificant Contamination
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No or insignificant contamination.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 1/3 of Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contamination is greater than one third of the total area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2/3 of Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contamination is greater than two thirds of the total area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 1/3 to 2/3 of Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 1/3 to 2/3 of Area

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Contamination
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No contamination.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Width
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A measurement of the shorter of two linear axis.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Conveyor
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of conveyor used for moving goods from one location to another.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aerial Cableway
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A transportation system consisting of load cables strung between pylons on which carrier units (for example: cars or buckets intended to transport people, material, and/or equipment) are suspended.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Belt Conveyor
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A conveyor along which material or people are transported by means of a moving belt.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flume
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An artificial channel, usually an inclined chute or trough, for carrying water to furnish power, transport logs down a mountainside, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lift/Elevator
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of various mechanical devices for raising objects or materials.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Station Name
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The name of the reference tide station with reference water level for tidal stream panel observations.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Data Assessment
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The categorization of the assessment level of bathymetric data for an area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Assessed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The quality of the bathymetric data has been assessed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Assessed (Oceanic)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The quality of oceanic bathymetric data (depths deeper than 200 metres) has been assessed, however details are not required.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unassessed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Not having been assessed.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minimum Ice Type
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Specifies the minimum thickness of the ice in centimetres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Condition
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The various conditions of buildings and other constructions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Under Construction
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Being built but not yet capable of function.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ruined
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure in a decayed or deteriorated condition resulting from neglect or disuse, or a damaged structure in need of repair.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Under Reclamation
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area of the sea, a lake or the navigable part of a river that is being reclaimed as land, usually by the dumping of earth and other material.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Not in Use
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Use has ceased, but the facility still exists intact; disused.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Planned Construction
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Detailed planning has been completed but construction has not been initiated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Operational
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: completed, undamaged and working normally.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Breccia for the Third Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. Describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the third partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the third partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Clearance Length
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The length of a feature, such as a lock or basin, which is available for safe navigation. This may, or may not, be the same as the total physical length of the feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Value of Magnetic Variation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The angle between the magnetic and geographical meridians at any place, expressed in degrees east or west to indicate the direction of magnetic north from true north.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Current Scour Dimensions
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The length, width, depth and orientation of the longest dimension of a scour that is associated with the object and that is caused by the action of currents.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Reference Direction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A direction used as a basis for comparison of other directions.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: National Maritime Authority
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The country responsible for establishing the maritime area and its purpose

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Edition Number
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Edition of the ENC being referenced.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Controlling Authority
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The recognised authority responsible for establishing and maintaining the administrative affairs of all matters relating to a particular field or subject.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Production Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of an area set aside for heavy industry.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Quarry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An open-air excavation for the extraction of stone intended principally for use in construction.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mine
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An excavation made in the terrain for the purpose of extracting and/or exploiting natural resources.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stockpile
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A reserve stock of material, equipment or other supplies.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Power Station Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A facility including one or more buildings and equipment used for power generation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Refinery Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A facility where petroleum and/or petroleum products are refined.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Timber Yard
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An open tract for the storage of wooden lumber and timbers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Factory Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A group of buildings where goods are manufactured.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Tank Farm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A collection of collocated large-capacity tanks in which petroleum, natural gas, or liquid petrochemicals are stored.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wind Farm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A collection of wind turbines that are collocated and are organized as a single power generation unit.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slag Heap/Spoil Heap
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Hill of refuse from a mine, industrial plant etc. on land.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Production Plant
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A plant where production takes place.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Solar Farm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large-scale photovoltaic system (PV system) designed for the supply of merchant power into the electricity grid. They are differentiated from most building-mounted and other decentralised solar power applications because they supply power at the utility level, rather than to a local user or users. The generic expression utility-scale solar is sometimes used to describe this type of project.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Left Q-Route Width
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The left-hand channel width of a Q-Route expressed as the measurement taken from the route centreline to the channel limit when proceeding UP a Q-route (e.g. A to B to C to D).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Bottom Vertical Safety Separation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A percentage value that can be applied to a charted depth in order to establish the BVSS clearance.

S100FC:uom.S100Base:name: percent
S100FC:uom.S100Base:definition: by a specified amount in or for every hundred

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Boundary Status Type
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Identifies the status of a boundary

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Definite
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A boundry having an established, accepted delimitation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Indefinite
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A boundry that is vaguely delimited, so as to question the accurate delineation of territory and its depiction on cartographic products.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Defined Boundary
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Has not been defined by either of the adjoining authorities.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Not Yet Ratified
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Boundary has not been ratified

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Value of Nominal Range
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The luminous range of a light in a homogenous atmosphere in which the meteorological visibility is 10 sea miles.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: International Defence Organization (IDO) status
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The International Defence Organization (IDO) status (if applicable) that must precede, and be applied to, the Protective Marking thus making it an IDO Marking.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, also called the North Atlantic Alliance, is an intergovernmental military alliance.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Orientation Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The angular distance measured from true north to the major axis of the feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Depth Units
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The system of measurement used to define the depth.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Metres
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The basic unit of length in the International System of Units (SI) system.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Periodic Date Start
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The start of the active period for a seasonal object (for example a buoy).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Bridge Function
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A specific role that describes the purpose of a bridge.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vehicular
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Of, relating to, or designed for vehicles and especially motor vehicles.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rail
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Of, relating to, or designed for vehicles that run on a guiding track(s), especially trains.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pedestrian
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Of, relating to, or designed for walking.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aqueduct
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A bridge supporting an artificially elevated channel, for the conveyance of water.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Bridge Construction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The bridge’s primary shape and/or construction material.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Arch
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A typically curved structural member spanning an opening and serving as a support (as for the wall or other weight above the opening).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Viaduct
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure consisting of a series of arches or towers supporting a roadway, waterway, etc., across a depression, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pontoon Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A fixed floating bridge supported by pontoons.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Suspension Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A fixed bridge consisting of either a roadway or a truss suspended from two or more cables which pass over towers and are anchored by backstays to a firm foundation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Transporter Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Consists of towers on each side of the watercourse connected by a system of girders on which a carriage runs.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category Of Imagery
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The type of imagery produced by techniques used to obtain, process, or interpret images created by different types of radiation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aerial Photograph
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any photograph taken from the air. Sometimes called air photograph.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ground Imagery
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A photograph taken by a camera located on the ground.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Oblique Photograph
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A photograph taken with the camera axis intentionally directed between the horizontal and the vertical.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Panoramic Imagery
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A wide angle view, generally taken by rotation about an axis.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Satellite Image
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Image produced by satellite orbiting the earth.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Surrounding Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The depth value determined for seabed around an underwater hazard, based on the depth of the surrounding area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Depth Range Maximum Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The maximum (deepest) value of a depth range.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Major Light
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A statement expressing if a light is considered to be a major light in terms of ECDIS display in a particular area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Uncertainty Fixed
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The best estimate of the fixed horizontal or vertical accuracy component for positions, depths, heights, vertical distances and vertical clearances.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Iceberg Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Specifies the total concentration of icebergs in an area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 45 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is greater than 45 Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 15 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is greater than 15 Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 15-44 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between fifteen and forty four Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 10-44 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between ten and forty four Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 10-14 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between ten and fourteen Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 7-14 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between seven and fourteen Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 7-10 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between seven and ten Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 5-10 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between five and ten Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 5-6 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between five and six Nautical Mile between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 3-6 nm Between Bergs
