S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between three and six Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 3-4 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between three and four Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 1-4 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between one and four Nautical Mile between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 1-2 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between one and two Nautical Mile between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 0.5-2.0 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between half and two Nautical Mile between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 0.5-1.0 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is between half and one Nautical Mile between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 1.0 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is less than 1 Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 0.5 nm Between Bergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Iceberg concentration is less than 0.5 Nautical Miles between icebergs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Icebergs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An absence of massive pieces of ice of varying shape, protruding more than 5 m above sea-level, which have broken away from a glacier or an ice shelf, and which may be afloat or aground.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Military Practice Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of area by military use.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Torpedo Exercise Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which exercises are carried out with torpedoes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Submarine Exercise Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which submarine exercises are carried out.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Firing Danger Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Areas for bombing and missile exercises.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mine-Laying Practice Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which mine laying exercises are carried out.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Arms Firing Range
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area for shooting pistols, rifles and machine guns etc. at a target.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: ACLANT Grid
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ACLANT (Allied Command Atlantic) submarine grid provides NATO submarine operating authorities with a common grid for the water space management of NATO submarines.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Surface Danger Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which certain activities or factors of significance to surface navigation or operations apply.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: JMC Areas - JENOA Grid
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A Joint Exercise Notification and Operating Area management grid used by the Joint Maritime Operational Training Staff (JMOTS) for the positioning of forces. It provides a framework for operating forces in widely dispersed groups.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Safe Bottoming Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area that has been surveyed and reported as safe for submarines to rest on the sea bed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Submarine Danger Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which submarine operations are prohibited or limited, owing to the existence of hazards to dived submarines.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Testing and Evaluation Range
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified zone for the provision of sonar calibration or other underwater testing.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Impact Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area allocated for bombardment during the live firing of weapons.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Live Fire Range
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area used for live firing of weapons to bombard a designated area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minelike Echo Density
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Density of mine-like echoes per square mile.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Data Available
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No data available.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Light Milecs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Light - 1-20 Milecs/sq mile.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Milecs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Medium - 21-40 Milecs/sq mile.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Heavy Milecs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Heavy - 41-70 Milecs/sq mile.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Heavy Milecs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Very Heavy -71 Milecs/sq mile and more.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minimum Berth Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The least depth of the body of water at the berth or in a berth pocket adjacent to the berth.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minimum Flight Level
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A minimum surface of constant atmospheric pressure which is related to a specific pressure datum, (1,013.2 hectopascal (hPa) or 29.92 inches) and is separated from the consecutive flight levels by a pressure interval corresponding to 500 feet (152.4 m.)

S100FC:uom.S100Base:name: foot
S100FC:uom.S100Base:definition: a unit of length equal to 12 inches, 1/6 of a fathom, or 30.480 centimetres

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Average Thickness
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Defines the average thickness of the ice in centimetres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Height of Iceberg Topside
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Defines the maximum height of an iceberg above the waterline in metres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Type Of Resource Location
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The type of resource that is located in a particular location.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Potable Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Water which can be used for drinking and food preparation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Engineer Resources
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Location where building materials are available.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Depot
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Location suitable for bulk storage, eg. a fuel dump. (AML)

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Attenuation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A lessening in amount, particularly the reduction of the amplitude of a wave or the intensity of light or sound with distance from the origin.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Optimum Display Scale
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The largest intended viewing scale for the data.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minimum Display Scale
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The smallest intended viewing scale for the data.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Pipeline/Pipe
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of a pipe systems use.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Outfall Pipe
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pipe (generally a sewer or drainage pipe) discharging into the sea or a river.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Intake Pipe
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pipe taking water from a river or other body of water, to drive a mill or supply a canal, waterworks, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sewer
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pipe in a sewage system for carrying water or sewage to a disposal area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bubbler System
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A submerged pipe from which warm water bubbles, preventing the surrounding water from freezing.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Supply Pipe
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pipe used for transport (supply) of gas or liquid product.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bubble Curtain
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A high pressure sub-surface pipeline (usually on the seafloor) with holes emitting a curtain of air bubbles. Its uses include: the prevention of acoustic transmission through the water; preventing the spread of surface debris or floating liquids; controlling the movement of fish.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Communication Channel
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A channel number assigned to a specific radio frequency, frequencies or frequency band.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Date Disused
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The date that an entity ceases to be used.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Vertical Datum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The reference level used for expressing the vertical measurements of points on the earth's surface. Also called datum level, reference plane, levelling datum, datum for sounding reduction, datum for heights.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Low Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of the low waters of spring tides. This level is used as a tidal datum in some areas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Lower Low Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of lower low water springs at a place.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Sea Level
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of the surface of the sea at a tide station for all stages of the tide over a 19-year period, usually determined from hourly height readings measured from a fixed predetermined reference level.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lowest Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level conforming to the lowest tide observed at a place, or somewhat lower.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of all low waters at a place over a 19-year period.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lowest Low Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level conforming to the lowest water level observed at a place at spring tides during a period of time shorter than 19 years.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Approximate Mean Low Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, usually within 0.3m from that of Mean Low Water Springs (MLWS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Indian Spring Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary tidal datum approximating the level of the mean of the lower low water at spring tides. It was first used in waters surrounding India.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Low Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, approximating that of mean low water springs (MLWS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Approximate Lowest Astronomical Tide
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, usually within 0.3m from that of Lowest Astronomical Tide (LAT).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nearly Lowest Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level approximating the lowest water level observed at a place, usually equivalent to the Indian Spring Low Water (ISLW).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Lower Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of the lower low waters at a place over a 19-year period.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The lowest level reached at a place by the water surface in one oscillation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Approximate Mean Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, usually within 0.3m from that of Mean Low Water (MLW).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Approximate Mean Lower Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, usually within 0.3m from that of Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of all high waters at a place over a 19-year period.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean High Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of the high waters of spring tides.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The highest level reached at a place by the water surface in one oscillation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Approximate Mean Sea Level
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, usually within 0.3m from that of Mean Sea Level (MSL).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: High Water Springs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level, approximating that of mean high water springs (MHWS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Higher High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average height of higher high waters at a place over a 19-year period.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Equinoctial Spring Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The level of low water springs near the time of an equinox.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lowest Astronomical Tide
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The lowest tide level which can be predicted to occur under average meteorological conditions and under any combination of astronomical conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Local Datum
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary datum defined by a local harbour authority, from which levels and tidal heights are measured by this authority.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: International Great Lakes Datum 1985
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A vertical reference system with its zero based on the mean water level at Rimouski/Pointe-au-Père, Quebec, over the period 1970 to 1988.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Water Level
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average of all hourly water levels over the available period of record.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lower Low Water Large Tide
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average of the lowest low waters, one from each of 19 years of observations.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Higher High Water Large Tide
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The average of the highest high waters, one from each of 19 years of observations.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nearly Highest High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arbitrary level approximating the highest water level observed at a place, usually equivalent to the high water springs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Highest Astronomical Tide
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The highest tidal level which can be predicted to occur under average meteorological conditions and under any combination of astronomical conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Local High Water Reference Level
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: High water reference level of the local area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Baltic Sea Chart Datum 2000
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The datum refers to each Baltic country's realization of the European Vertical Reference System (EVRS) with land-uplift epoch 2000, which is connected to the Normaal Amsterdams Peil (NAP).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mean Tide Level
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: (MTL) - the level mid-way between one or more successive high and low waters. It may be computed by averaging the four tidal levels (MHWS, MHWN, MLWN and MLWS or MHHW, MLHW, MHLW and MLLW) for the place concerned.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Copyright Statement
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates any copyright or releaseability restrictions on the data.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Name
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The individual name of a feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Beacon Shape
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes the characteristic geometric form of the beacon.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stake, Pole, Perch, Post
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An elongated wood or metal pole, driven into the ground or seabed, which serves as a navigational aid or a support for a navigational aid.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Withy
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tree without roots stuck or spoiled into the bottom of the sea to serve as a navigational aid.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Beacon Tower
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A solid structure of the order of 10 metres in height used as a navigational aid.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lattice Beacon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure consisting of strips of metal or wood crossed or interlaced to form a structure to serve as an aid to navigation or as a support for an aid to navigation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pile Beacon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A long heavy timber(s) or section(s) of steel, wood, concrete, etc., forced into the seabed to serve as an aid to navigation or as a support for an aid to navigation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cairn
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A mound of stones, usually conical or pyramidal, raised as a landmark or to designate a point of importance in surveying.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Buoyant Beacon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tall spar-like beacon fitted with a permanently submerged buoyancy chamber, the lower end of the body is secured to seabed sinker either by a flexible joint or by a cable under tension.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Speed Maximum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction. Speed maximum is the maximum rate of travel that can occur.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Exhibition Condition of Light
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The outward display of the light.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Light Shown Without Change of Character
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light shown throughout the 24 hours without change of character.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Daytime Light
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light which is only exhibited by day.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fog Light
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light which is exhibited in fog or conditions of reduced visibility.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Night Light
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A light which is only exhibited at night.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Production Agency
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The organization or agency responsible for producing the source.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Obstruction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of objects that impede movement.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Snag/Stump
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tree, branch or broken pile embedded in the ocean floor, river or lake bottom and not visible on the surface, forming thereby a hazard to vessels.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wellhead
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A submarine structure projecting some distance above the seabed and capping a temporarily abandoned or suspended oil or gas well.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Diffuser
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure on an outfall through which liquids are discharged. The structure will usually project above the level of the outfall and can be an obstruction to navigation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Crib
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A permanent marine structure usually designed to support or elevate pipelines; especially a structure enclosing a screening device at the offshore end of a potable water intake pipe. The structure is commonly a heavy timber enclosure that has been sunken with rocks or other debris.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish Haven
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Areas established by private interests, usually sport fishermen, to simulate natural reefs and wrecks that attract fish. The reefs are constructed by dumping assorted junk in areas which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Foul Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area of numerous unidentified dangers to navigation. The area serves as a warning to the mariner that all dangers are not identified individually and that navigation through the area may be hazardous.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Boom
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Floating barriers, anchored to the bottom, used to deflect the path of floating ice in order to prevent the obstruction of locks, intakes, etc., and to prevent damage to bridge piers and other structures.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ground Tackle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Equipment such as anchors, concrete blocks, chains and cables, etc., used to position floating structures such as trot and mooring buoys etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Boom
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A floating barrier used to protect a river or harbour mouth or to create a sheltered area for storage purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wave Energy Device
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A device to extract energy from the surface motion of ocean waves or from pressure fluctuations below the surface.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Subsurface Ocean Data Acquisition System
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A submerged device, not being a ship, together with its appurtenant equipment, deployed at sea essentially for the purpose of collecting, storing or transmitting samples or data relating to the marine environment.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Artificial Reef
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A man-made structure that may mimic some of the characteristics of a natural reef, intended to attract sea life.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Template
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure placed on the seafloor below a drilling rig to guide the drill.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Manifold
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large steel structure up to 20 metres in height above the seafloor, or a steel frame secured to the seafloor with piles to anchor the end of a submarine pipeline, for delivery to a production platform.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Submerged Pingo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A hill of soil-covered ice pushed up by hydrostatic pressure in an area of permafrost that is located underwater.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Remains of Platform
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The distributed remains of a platform.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Scientific Instrument
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An instrument used for scientific purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Underwater Turbine
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of various machines having a rotor, usually with vanes or blades, driven by the pressure, momentum, or reactive thrust of a moving fluid, as steam, water, hot gases, or air, either occurring in the form of free jets or as a fluid passing through and entirely filling a housing around the rotor and is located underwater.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Active Submarine Volcano
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An active seabed volcano, which may be submerged or projecting above the water at the chart sounding datum.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shark Net
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A submerged net placed around beaches to reduce shark attacks on swimmers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mangrove
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: One of several genera of tropical trees or shrubs which produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying coasts into shallow water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Well Protection Structure
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure, typically a dome or cube, erected over a wellhead or equipment attached to it (a tree) to lessen the danger of vessels snagging gear.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Subsea Installation
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any oil or gas related installation or structure on, or projecting from, the seabed, for example a submerged platform or concrete foundations.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pipeline Obstruction
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any pipeline related structure which projects above the seabed, for example a joint, T-piece, valve or sleeve, or a crossing where one pipeline is raised over another by means of a supporting structure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Free Standing Conductor Pipe
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Lengths of large diameter casing pipe projecting from a wellhead which may extend only a short distance above the seabed, or rise to project above the sea surface.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Storage Tank
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: large seabed structures, typically made of concrete, capable of storing oil or gas and usually found attached or adjacent to a rig, or marked by a single point mooring buoy. (AML)

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pontoon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A floating structure, usually rectangular in shape which serves as landing, pier head, bridge support, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sundry Objects
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Miscellaneous items and objects, most of which have been lost overboard or otherwise abandoned to the sea, for example cargo containers or vehicles.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: File Reference
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The file name of an externally referenced text file.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category Of Military Exercise Airspace
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The type of military exercise airspace that is being depicted.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Linkage
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Location (address) for online access using a URL/URI address or similar addressing scheme.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Abandonment Date
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The date on which a borehole is sealed. All well-head equipment is removed and the hole plugged with cement and a steel plate cemented over the top.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Type Of Military Activity
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Type of military activity or activities associated with area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Name of Resource
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Name of the online resource.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Value of Maximum Range
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The extreme distance at which a feature can be seen or a signal detected.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Direction of Sastrugi
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the bearing of a sastrugi. Sastrugi: complex, fragile shapes of snow on top of sea ice that resemble sand dunes; they form parallel to the prevailing wind direction; sastrugi can also form on snow cover over land.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Sastrugi
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Absence of sharp irregular grooves or ridges formed on a snow surface by wind erosion, saltation of snow particles, and deposition.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: North
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 348.75-011.25 degrees (true north).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Variable
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Subject to variation or changes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Nature of Construction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The building's primary construction material.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Masonry
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed of stones or bricks, usually quarried, shaped, and mortared.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Concreted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed of concrete, a material made of sand and gravel that is united by cement into a hardened mass used for roads, foundations, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Loose Boulders
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed from large stones or blocks of concrete, often placed loosely for protection against waves or water turbulence.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hard Surfaced
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed with a surface of hard material, usually a term applied to roads surfaced with asphalt or concrete.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unsurfaced
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed with no extra protection, usually a term applied to roads not surfaced with a hard material.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wooden
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed from wood.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Metal
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed from metal.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Glass Reinforced Plastic
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Constructed from a plastic material strengthened with fibres of glass.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Latticed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure of crossed wooden or metal strips usually arranged to form a diagonal pattern of open spaces between the strips.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Glass
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: [1] Any artificial or natural substance having similar properties and composition, as fused borax, obsidian, or the like. [2] Something made of such a substance, as a windowpane.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Based On Fixed Marks
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A straight route (known as a recommended track, range or leading line), which comprises: a. at least two structures (usually beacons or daymarks) and/or natural features, which may carry lights and/or top-marks. The structures/features are positioned so that when observed to be in line, a vessel can follow a known bearing with safety. (Adapted from International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA Aids to Navigation Guide, 1990); or b. a single structure or natural feature, which may carry lights and/or a topmark, and a specified bearing which can be followed with safety. (S-57 Edition 3.1, Appendix A Chapter 2, Page 2.72, November 2000, as amended).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Buoy Shape
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The principal shape and/or design of a buoy.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Conical
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has approximately the shape or the appearance of a pointed cone with the point upwards.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Can
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the shape of a cylinder, or a truncated cone that approximates to a cylinder, with a flat end uppermost.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Spherical
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Shaped like a sphere, which is a body the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pillar
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure is a narrow vertical structure, pillar or lattice tower.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Spar
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the form of a pole, or of a very long cylinder, floating upright.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Barrel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The upper part of the body above the water-line, or the greater part of the superstructure, has the form of a barrel or cylinder floating horizontally.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Superbuoy
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A very large buoy designed to carry a signal light of high luminous intensity at a high elevation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Buoy
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specially constructed shuttle shaped buoy which is used in ice conditions.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Number of Icebergs in Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the number of Icebergs within a specified area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Length
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A measurement of the longer of two linear axis.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Attribute Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Specifies the areas of ice of specific age or arrangement which comprise only part of the total concentration of ice in an area ('Ca,Cb,and Cc).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Free
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Water surface completely free of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Open Water (1/10 Ice)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large area of freely navigable water in which sea ice is present in concentrations less than 1/10 and ice of land origin is absent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bergy Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large area of navigable water in which ice of land origin is present or possible at a total concentration less than 1/10.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Traffic Flow
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Direction of vessels passing a reference point.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Inbound
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Traffic flow in a general direction toward a port or similar destination.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Outbound
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Traffic flow in a general direction away from a port or similar point of origin.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: One-Way
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Traffic flow in one general direction only.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Two-Way
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Traffic flow in two generally opposite directions.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Lead (or Fracture or Crack) Width
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the width of a lead or fracture or crack in metres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Strength Of Magnetic Anomaly
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indication of the strength of the magnetic anomaly caused by the object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nil Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has no magnetic reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a slight reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a moderate magnetic reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Strong Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a strong magnetic reading.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Breccia for the Second Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. Describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the second partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the second partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Keel Maximum Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the maximum depth of ice keels in decimetres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: ICAO Code
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: An airfield unique location identifier designated by the International Civil Aviation Organisation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Anchorage
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of an area where different use types of vessel can remain static.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unrestricted Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Deep Water Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels of deep draught anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Tanker Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which tankers anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Quarantine Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area where a vessel anchors when satisfying quarantine regulations.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Seaplane Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which seaplanes anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Craft Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which yachts and small boats anchor or may anchor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Anchorage for Periods Up To 24 Hours
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor for periods of up to 24 hours.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Anchorage for a Limited Period of Time
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels may anchor for a period of time not to exceed a specific limit.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Waiting Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which vessels anchor or may anchor while waiting, for example, for access to a port or berth.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Reported Anchorage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A location not defined by a regulatory authority that has been reported to be suitable and safe for anchoring.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Built-Up Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Human settlement classification.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Urban Area
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area predominantly occupied by man-made structures used for residential, commercial, and industrial purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Settlement
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A continuously occupied concentration of tents or lightweight fixed structures (for example: huts) serving as residences.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Village
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A self-contained group of houses and associated buildings, usually in a country area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Town
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An inhabited place larger and more regularly built and with more complete and independent local government than a village but not incorporated as a city.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: City
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A major town inhabited by a large permanent community with all essential services.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Holiday Village
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A complex for holiday-makers with cottages, shops, and entertainment, on site, which is mainly populated on a seasonal basis.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Buried Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The depth below the seabed to which an object is buried.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Clearance Width
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The width of a feature, such as a lock or basin, which is available for safe navigation. This may, or may not, be the same as the total physical width of the feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Cargo
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the different types of cargo that a ship may be carrying.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bulk
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Unpacked homogenous cargo poured loose in a certain space of a vessel, for example oil or grain.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Container
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: One of a number of standard sized cargo carrying units, secured using standard corner attachments and bar.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: General
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Break bulk cargo normally loaded by crane.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Liquid
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any cargo loaded by pipeline.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Passenger
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A fee paying traveller.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Livestock
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Live animals carried in bulk.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dangerous or Hazardous
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Dangerous or hazardous cargo as described by the IMO International Maritime Dangerous Goods code.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Heavy Lift
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Indivisible heavy items of weight generally over 100 tons, and width or height greater than 100 metres.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ballast
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Material carried by a ship to ensure its stability.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dry Bulk Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Commodity cargo that is transported unpackaged in large quantities. These types of goods usually need to be kept dry during the whole transportation period.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Liquid Bulk Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Liquids or gases that are transported in bulk and carried unpackaged.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Reefer Container Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Cargo transported in refrigerated containers, generally perishable commodities which require temperature-controlled transportation, such as fruit, meat, fish, vegetables, dairy products and other foods.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ro-Ro Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Wheeled cargo, such as cars, busses, trucks, agricultural vehicles and cranes, that are driven on and off the ship on their own wheels or using a platform vehicle, such as a self-propelled modular transporter.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Project Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Project cargo is a term used to broadly describe the national or international transportation of large, heavy, high value, or critical (to the project they are intended for) pieces of equipment. Also commonly referred to as heavy lift, this includes shipments made of various components which need disassembly for shipment and reassembly after delivery.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Break Bulk Cargo
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Goods that are stowed on board ship in individually counted units, and not in intermodal containers nor in bulk as with oil or grain.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Surf Height
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Average height of the surf.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Depth Restriction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Restrictions and/or additional qualifying information relating to submarine navigation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Orientation of Leads or Fractures
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the predominant orientation of ice leads and fractures.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Leads or Fractures
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: There are no rectilinear or wedge-shaped cracks more than 50 metres wide from several kilometres to several hundreds of kilometres in length; and no breaks or ruptures through close ice, compact ice, consolidated ice, fast ice, or a single floe resulting from shears and deformation processes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: North
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 348.75-011.25 degrees (true north).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Variable
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Subject to variation or changes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Zone of Confidence In Data
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the zone of confidence in data within an area based on the positional accuracy, survey equipment and coverage.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence A1
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Positional Accuracy +/- 5 metres + 5% depth; Depth Accuracy 0.5 metre + 1% depth; Full area search undertaken. Significant seafloor features detected and depths measured; Controlled, systematic survey, high position and depth accuracy achieved using DGPS or a minimum three high quality lines of position (LOP) and a multibeam, channel or mechanical sweep system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence A2
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Positional Accuracy +/- 20 metres; Depth Accuracy 1.0 metre + 2% depth; Full area search undertaken. Significant seafloor features detected and depths measured; Controlled, systematic survey achieving position and depth accuracy less than ZOC A1 and using a modern survey echosounder and a sonar or mechanical sweep system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence B
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Positional Accuracy +/- 50 metres; Depth Accuracy 1.0 metre + 2% depth; Full area search not achieved, uncharted features hazardous to surface navigation are not expected but may exist; Controlled, systematic survey achieving similar depth but lesser position accuracies than ZOCA2, using a modern survey echosounder, but no sonar or mechanical sweep system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence C
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Positional Accuracy +/- 500 metres; Depth Accuracy 2.0 metre + 5% depth; Full area search not achieved, depth anomalies may be expected; Low accuracy survey or data collected on an opportunity basis such as soundings on passage.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence D
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Positional Accuracy worse than ZOC C; Depth Accuracy worse than ZOC C; Full area search not achieved, large depth anomalies may be expected; Poor quality data or data that cannot be quality assessed due to lack of information.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Zone of Confidence U
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The quality of the bathymetric data has yet to be assessed.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Drift Direction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The direction of displacement of ice floes and other ice features resulting from the impact of wind and currents including tidal currents and of forces transferred through the ice cover from other regions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Ice Motion
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Absence of ice drift, shearing, fracturing, compacting, compression or diverging.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to NE
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the North East.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to E
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the East.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to SE
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the South East.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to S
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the South.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to SW
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the South West.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to W
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the West.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to NW
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the North West.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Drift to N
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The direction of ice drift is to the North.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Variable
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Subject to variation or changes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Marks Navigational - System Of
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The system of navigational buoyage a region complies with.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IALA A
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Navigational aids conform to the International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA A system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IALA B
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Navigational aids conform to the International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA B system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No System
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Navigational aids do not conform to any defined system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Main European Inland Waterway Marking System
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Navigational aids as required in international, national or regional regulations that contain the same navigational aids as the European Code for Inland Waterways of UNECE, or if there is no regulation for a waterway, navigational aids as recommended in the European Code for Inland Waterways of UNECE

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Area Category
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Category of the designated area

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Solid Red
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The area is a scheduled Danger Area; for firings wholly within the area and within specified times, a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) is not required (AML).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pecked Red
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The area is a Notified Danger Area; for firings and other potentially hazardous activities, a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) is required (AML).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Fractures Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes the degree of disunity in an ice area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads Seldom Then in 10 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads seldom then in 10 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 5-10 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 5-10 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 3-5 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 3-5 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 2-3 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 2-3 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads Often Then in 2 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads often then in 2 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 1/10 to 3/10; Big Floes - 7/10 to 10/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 10 to 30 percent in small and medium floes and between 70 to 100 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 4/10 to 6/10; Big Floes - 4/10 to 6/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 40 to 60 percent in small and medium floes and between 40 to 60 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 7/10 to 10/10; Big Floes 1/10 to 3/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 70 to 100 percent in small and medium floes and between 10 to 30 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes Only
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains contiguous pieces of sea ice between 20 and 500 metres across only.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floes Only
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Small floes only.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Fractures
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: There are no breaks or ruptures through close ice, compact ice, consolidated ice, fast ice, or a single floe resulting from shears and deformation processes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Signal Generation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The mechanism used to generate a fog or light signal.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Radio Activated
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Activated by radio signal.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Call Activated
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Activated by making a call to a manned station.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Text
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A non-formatted digital text string.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Undetectable Mines Ratio
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The total fraction of undetectable mines.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Arc Extension
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: An indication that the default radius of a sector arc is to be extended by 5mm.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: IMO Adopted
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A defined maritime traffic route that has been adopted as an IMO routeing measure.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Value of Annual Change in Magnetic Variation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The annual change in magnetic variation values.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Target Reference Weight
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Reference weight of the target used when referring to burial probability.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lower Reference Weight
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Target weight is 500kg.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Higher Reference Weight
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Target weight is 1000kg.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Spudded Date
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The date on which a new well is spudded, meaning to start drilling a new borehole.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: First Detection Year
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The year in which the object was originally reported.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Function
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A specific role that describes a feature.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Harbour-Masters Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A local official who has charge of mooring and berthing of vessels, collecting harbour fees, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Customs Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Serves as a government office where customs duties are collected, the flow of goods are regulated and restrictions enforced, and shipments or vehicles are cleared for entering or leaving a country.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Health Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The office which is charged with the administration of health laws and sanitary inspections.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hospital
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An institution or establishment providing medical or surgical treatment for the ill or wounded.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Post Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The public department, agency or organisation responsible primarily for the collection, transmission and distribution of mail.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hotel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An establishment, especially of a comfortable or luxurious kind, where paying visitors are provided with accommodation, meals and other services.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Railway Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building with platforms where trains arrive, load, discharge and depart.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Police Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The headquarters of a local police force and that is where those under arrest are first charged.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Water-Police Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The headquarters of a local water-police force.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pilot Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The office or headquarters of pilots; the place where the services of a pilot may be obtained.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pilot Lookout
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A distinctive structure or place on shore from which personnel keep watch upon events at sea or along the coast.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bank Office
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An office for custody, deposit, loan, exchange or issue of money.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Headquarters for District Control
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The quarters of an executive officer (director, manager, etc.) with responsibility for an administrative area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Transit Shed/Warehouse
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building or part of a building for storage of wares or goods.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Factory
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building or buildings with equipment for manufacturing; a workshop.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Power Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A stationary plant containing apparatus for large scale conversion of some form of energy (such as hydraulic, steam, chemical or nuclear energy) into electrical energy.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Administrative
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building for the management of affairs.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Educational Facility
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An establishment for teaching and learning (for example school, college, university, etc).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Church
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building for public Christian worship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Chapel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place for Christian worship other than a parish, cathedral or church, especially one attached to a private house or institution.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Temple
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building for public Jewish worship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pagoda
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A Hindu or Buddhist temple or sacred building.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shinto Shrine
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building for public Shinto worship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Buddhist Temple
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building for public Buddhist worship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mosque
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A Muslim place of worship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Marabout
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A shrine marking the burial place of a Muslim holy man.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lookout
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Keeping a watch upon events at sea or along the coast.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Communication
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Transmitting and/or receiving electronic communication signals.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Television
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A system for reproducing on a screen visual images transmitted (usually with sound) by radio signals.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Radio
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Transmitting and/or receiving radio-frequency electromagnetic waves as a means of communication.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Radar
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A method, system or technique of using beamed, reflected, and timed radio waves for detecting, locating, or tracking objects, and for measuring altitudes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Light Support
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A structure serving as a support for one or more lights.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Microwave
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Broadcasting and receiving signals using microwaves.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cooling
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Generation of chilled liquid and/or gas for cooling purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Observation
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A place from which the surroundings can be observed but at which a watch is not habitually maintained.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Timeball
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A visual time signal in the form of a ball.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Clock
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Instrument for measuring time and recording hours.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Control
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Used to control the flow of traffic within a specified range of an installation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Airship Mooring
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Equipment or structure to secure an airship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stadium
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An arena for holding and viewing events.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bus Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building where buses and coaches regularly stop to take on and/or let off passengers, especially for long-distance travel.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sea Rescue Control
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A unit responsible for promoting efficient organization of search and rescue services and for coordinating the conduct of search and rescue operations within a search and rescue region.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Observatory
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building designed and equipped for making observations of astronomical, meteorological, or other natural phenomena.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ore Crusher
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building or structure used to crush ore.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Boathouse
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building or shed, usually built partly over water, for sheltering a boat or boats.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pumping Station
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A facility to move solids, liquids or gases by means of pressure or suction.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Operator
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Name of the company operating the installation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Time Relative to Tide
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The time difference relative to the reference tide.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Keel Mean Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the mean depth of ice keels in decimetres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Permitted Vessel Length
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The maximum length of a vessel permitted in a channel or dock, at a berth, or at an anchorage or mooring.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Sonar Signal Strength
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: An indication of the strength of the echo of a sonic signal returned from an object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nil Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object has a nil reading of described sensor type.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object has a slight reading of described sensor type.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object has a moderate reading of described sensor type.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Strong Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object has a strong reading of described sensor type.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Brash Ice
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Accumulation of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 meters (6.6 feet) across; the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads Seldom Then in 10 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads seldom then in 10 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 5-10 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 5-10 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 3-5 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 3-5 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads in 2-3 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads in 2-3 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Frequency of Cracks and Leads Often Then in 2 km on Route
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Frequency of cracks and leads often then in 2 km on route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 1/10 to 3/10; Big Floes - 7/10 to 10/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 10 to 30 percent in small and medium floes and between 70 to 100 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 4/10 to 6/10; Big Floes - 4/10 to 6/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 40 to 60 percent in small and medium floes and between 40 to 60 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes - 7/10 to 10/10; Big Floes 1/10 to 3/10 Concentration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractures occur in between 70 to 100 percent in small and medium floes and between 10 to 30 percent in large floes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small and Medium Floes Only
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains contiguous pieces of sea ice between 20 and 500 metres across only.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floes Only
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Small floes only.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Fractures
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: There are no breaks or ruptures through close ice, compact ice, consolidated ice, fast ice, or a single floe resulting from shears and deformation processes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Multiplicity Known
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The number of features of identical character that exist as a co-located group is or is not known.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Landing Conditions
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Description of the landing conditions including surface composition and immediate topographical features.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Trafficability
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Ability of the beach to support vehicular traffic.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Firm Trafficability
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Can be used by 2WD vehicles or 4WD vehicles and trailers unless heavy and continued use is intended.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Trafficability
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Can be used by military 3 or 4 tonne vehicles starting from rest in 4WD.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Soft Trafficability
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 4WD unable to start from rest but can cross soft patch if already on the move.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Soft Trafficability
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Impassable to wheeled vehicles, tracked vehicles may have difficulty.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Reference Year for Magnetic Variation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The reference calendar year for magnetic variation values.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Protective Marking
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A marking indicating the minimum standards of protection required of the data.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Top Secret
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains information classified at the Top Secret Level.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Secret
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains information classified at the ecret Level.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Confidential
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains information classified at the Confidential Level.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Information marked as "NATO Restricted" requires safeguards and protection from public release and disclosure. This category does not apply to information classified NATO Confidential, NATO SECRET or NATO COSMIC TOP SECRET.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unclassified
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Information marked as "NATO Unclassified" may only be used for official NATO purposes and may carry administrative or dissemination limitation markings.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Contains information with an unknown level of classification.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Reported Date
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The date that the item was observed, done, or investigated.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Magnetic Anomaly Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The value of the deviation from the normal magnetic variation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: In the Water
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: An indication if the feature is located in or over navigable water.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Compacting Strength
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: An indication of strength of the compacting of the ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Little Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Little compacting.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Pieces of floating ice subjected to a slight converging motion, which increases ice concentration and/or produces stresses which may result in ice deformation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight to Moderate Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Pieces of floating ice subjected to a slight to moderate converging motion, which increases ice concentration and/or produces stresses which may result in ice deformation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A moderate decrease in the separation between individual ice floes resulting in increased ice concentration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate to Strong Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A moderate to strong decrease in the separation between individual ice floes resulting in increased ice concentration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Strong Compacting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Floating ice pieces are subjected to a strong converging motion, which significantly increases ice concentration and/or produces stresses which are likely to result in ice deformation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Divergence
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice fields or floes in an area are subject to diverging or dispersive motion, thus reducing ice concentration and/or relieving stresses in the ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Marine Protected Area
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of marine protected areas based on IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources) categories.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category Ia
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Strict Nature Reserve: Protected area managed mainly for science.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category Ib
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Wilderness Area: Protected area managed mainly for wilderness protection.
