S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category II
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: National Park: Protected area managed mainly for ecosystem protection and recreation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category III
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Natural Monument: Protected area managed mainly for conservation of specific natural features.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category IV
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Habitat/Species Management Area: Protected area managed mainly for conservation through management intervention.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category V
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Protected Landscape/Seascape: Protected area managed mainly for landscape/seascape conservation and recreation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: IUCN Category VI
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Managed Resource Protected Area: Protected area managed mainly for the sustainable use of natural ecosystems.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Vessels Characteristics Unit
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The unit used for vessel characteristics attribute.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Metres
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The basic unit of length in the International System of Units (SI) system.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Metric Ton
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The tonne or metric ton (U.S.), often redundantly referred to as a metric tonne, is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kg (2,205 lb) or approximately the mass of one cubic metre of water at four degrees Celsius. It is sometimes abbreviated as mt in the United States, but this conflicts with other SI symbols. The tonne is not a unit in the International System of Units (SI), but is accepted for use with the SI. In SI units and prefixes, the tonne is a megagram (Mg). The Imperial and US customary units comparable to the tonne are both spelled ton in English, though they differ in mass. Pronunciation of tonne (the word used in the UK) and ton is usually identical, but is not too confusing unless accuracy is important as the tonne and UK long ton differ by only 1.6.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ton
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Long ton (weight ton or imperial ton) is the name for the unit called the "ton" in the avoirdupois or Imperial system of measurements, as used in the United Kingdom and several other Commonwealth countries. It has been mostly replaced by the tonne, and in the United States by the short ton. One long ton is equal to 2,240 pounds (1,016 kg) or 35 cubic feet (0.9911 m) of salt water with a density of 64 lb/ft (1.025 g/ml). It has some limited use in the United States, most commonly in measuring the displacement of ships, and was the unit prescribed for warships by the Washington Naval Treaty for example battleships were limited to a mass of 35,000 long tons (36,000 t; 39,000 ST).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Short Ton
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A unit of weight equal to 2,000 pounds (907.18474 kg). In the United States it is often called simply ton without distinguishing it from the metric ton (tonne, 1,000 kilograms) or the long ton (2,240 pounds / 1,016.0469088 kilograms); rather, the other two are specifically noted. There are, however, some US applications for which unspecified tons normally means long tons (for example, Navy ships) or metric tons (world grain production figures). Both the long and short ton are defined as 20 hundredweights, but a hundredweight is 100 pounds (45.359237 kg) in the US system (short or net hundredweight) and 112 pounds (50.80234544 kg) in the Imperial system (long or gross hundredweight).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Gross Ton
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Gross tonnage (GT) is a function of the volume of all ship's enclosed spaces (from keel to funnel) measured to the outside of the hull framing. There is a sliding scale factor. So GT is a kind of capacity-derived index that is used to rank a ship for purposes of determining manning, safety and other statutory requirements and is expressed simply as GT, which is a unitless entity, even though its derivation is tied to the cubic meter unit of volumetric capacity.Tonnage measurements are now governed by an IMO Convention (International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969 (London-Rules)), which applies to all ships built after July 1982. In accordance with the Convention, the correct term to use now is GT, which is a function of the moulded volume of all enclosed spaces of the ship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Net Ton
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Net tonnage (NT) is based on a calculation of the volume of all cargo spaces of the ship. It indicates a vessels earning space and is a function of the moulded volume of all cargo spaces of the ship.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Dolphin
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of a post or group of posts, used for mooring or warping a vessel.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mooring Dolphin
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used as a mooring point for vessels.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Deviation Dolphin
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A post or group of posts, which a vessel may swing around for compass adjustment.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Berthing Dolphin
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used to extend the berth of a vessel by providing extra mooring points.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fender or Breasting Dolphin
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A post or group of posts driven into the seabed or riverbed, used to assist in berthing of vessels by taking up some berthing loads; keep vessels from pressing against the pier structure; or to protect structures from possible impact by ships.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Active Period
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Details of the operating times/dates that restrict when an object is active or in use.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Keel Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes the concentration of ice keels beneath an ice area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Less than one tenth concentration (aerial coverage) of snow-covered ice in an ice area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Keels
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Absence of ice keels.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Language
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The method of human communication, either spoken or written, consisting of the use of words in a structured and conventional way.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Heading Up Bearing
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The horizontal direction heading up a Q-Route (e.g. A to B to C to D), expressed as the angular distance from true north. It is usually measured from 0 at the reference direction clockwise through 360

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Signal Status
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The indication of an element of a signal sequence being a period of light/sound or eclipse/silence.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lit/Sound
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The indication of an element of a signal sequence being a period of light or sound.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Eclipsed/Silent
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The indication of an element of a signal sequence being a period of eclipse or silence.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Breccia for the First Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Ice breccia is pieces of ice of different ages frozen together. Describes the combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the first partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations plus the age of the younger ice consolidating the main pieces are allowed to describe the ice in the first partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Road
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of a road based on size.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Motorway
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A limited access dual carriageway road specially designed for fast long-distance traffic and subject to special regulations concerning its use. It may have more than two lanes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Major Road
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A hard surfaced (metalled) road; a main through route.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Minor Road
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A secondary road for local traffic.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Track/Path
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Track - a rough path or way formed by use. Path - a way or track laid down for walking or made by continual treading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Major Street
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A main road, in an urban area, for through traffic.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Minor Street
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A secondary road, in an urban area, for local traffic.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Reference Tide
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The reference tide to which the series of tidal stream values apply.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: High Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The highest level reached at a place by the water surface in one oscillation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Low Water
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The lowest level reached at a place by the water surface in one oscillation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Visual Prominence
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The extent to which a feature, either natural or artificial, is visible from seaward.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Visually Conspicuous
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Term applied to an object either natural or artificial which is distinctly and notably visible from seaward.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Not Visually Conspicuous
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An object that may be visible from seaward, but cannot be used as a fixing mark and is not conspicuous.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Prominent
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Objects which are easily identifiable, but do not justify being classed as conspicuous.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Survey Type
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the different survey types.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Reconnaissance/Sketch Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey made (due to lack of time or facilities) to a lower degree of accuracy and detail than the chosen scale would normally indicate.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thorough survey usually conducted with reference to guidelines.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Examination Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey principally aimed at the investigation of underwater obstructions and dangers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Passage Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey where soundings are acquired by vessels on passage.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Remotely Sensed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey where features have been positioned and delimited using remote sensing techniques.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Full Coverage
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey achieving 100% coverage using systematic, controlled techniques providing full seafloor coverage or full coverage to a defined depth and an investigation of all contacts.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Systematic Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A controlled survey but full coverage may not have been achieved.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Non-Systematic Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey of lower quality than a full coverage and systematic survey. Such surveys may be further categorized as reconnaissance, sketch, track, passage, remotely sensed and spot-sounding surveys.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Inadequately Surveyed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Not surveyed to modern standards; or due to its age, scale, or positional or vertical uncertainties is not suitable to the type of navigation expected in the area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Spot-Sounding Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A survey that uses a regular (for example grid) or irregular pattern of soundings obtained one at a time, and normally with very wide spacing.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Acoustically Swept Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A controlled, systematic survey to standard accuracy; using modern survey echo sounder with sonar sweep.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mechanically Swept Survey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Swept areas where the clearance depth is accurately known but the actual seabed depth is not accurately known.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Topmark/Daymark Shape
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The shape a topmark or daymark exhibits.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cone (Point Up)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Is where the vertex points up.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cone (Point Down)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Is where the vertex points down.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sphere
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A curved surface all points of which are equidistant from a fixed point within, called the centre.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2 Spheres
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Two spheres, one above the other. Two black spheres are commonly used as an International Association of Lighthouse Authorities - IALA topmark (isolated danger).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cylinder
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A solid geometrical figure generated by straight lines fixed in direction and describing with one of point a closed curve, especially a circle (in which case the figure is circular cylinder, its ends being parallel circles).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Board
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Usually of rectangular shape, made from timber or metal and used to provide a contrast with the natural background of a daymark. The actual daymark is often painted on to this board.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: X-Shaped
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having a shape or a cross-section like the capital letter X.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Upright Cross
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A cross with one vertical member and one horizontal member; that is, similar in shape to the character '+'.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cube (Point Up)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A cube standing on one of its vertexes. A cube is a solid contained by six equal squares, a regular hexahedron.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2 Cones (Point to Point)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 2 cones, one above the other, with their vertices together in the centre.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2 Cones (Base to Base)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 2 cones, one above the other, with their bases together in the centre and their vertices pointing up and down.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rhombus
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A plane figure having four equal sides and equal opposite angles (two acute and two obtuse); an oblique equilateral parallelogram.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2 Cones (Points Upward)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 2 cones, one above the other, with their vertices pointing up.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 2 Cones (Points Downward)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 2 cones, one above the other, with their vertices pointing down.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Besom (Point Up)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A bundle of rods or twigs. A besom, point up is where the thicker (untied) end of the besom is at the bottom.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Besom (Point Down)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A bundle of rods or twigs. A besom, point down is where the thinner (tied) end of the besom is at the bottom.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flag
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A flag mounted on a short pole.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sphere Over a Rhombus
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A sphere located above a rhombus.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Square
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A plane figure with four right angles and four equal straight sides.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rectangle (Horizontal)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A horizontal rectangle is where the two longer opposite sides are standing horizontally.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rectangle (Vertical)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rectangle is a plane figure with four right angles and four straight sides, opposite sides being parallel and equal in length. A vertical rectangle is where the two longer opposite sides are standing vertically.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Trapezium (Up)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A quadrilateral having one pair of opposite sides parallel, and which stands on its longer parallel side.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Trapezium (Down)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A quadrilateral having one pair of opposite sides parallel, and which stands on its shorter parallel side.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Triangle (Point Up)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A figure having three angles and three sides, and which has a vertex at the top.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Triangle (Point Down)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A figure having three angles and three sides, and which has a side at the top.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Circle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A perfectly round plane figure whose circumference is everywhere equidistant from its centre.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Two Upright Crosses (One Over the Other)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Two upright crosses, generally vertically disposed one above the other.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: T-Shape
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having a shape like the capital letter T.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Triangle Pointing Up Over a Circle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A triangle, vertex uppermost, located above a circle.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Upright Cross Over a Circle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An upright cross located above a circle.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rhombus Over a Circle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rhombus located above a circle.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Circle Over a Triangle Pointing Up
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A circle located over a triangle, vertex uppermost.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Other Shape (See Shape Information)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An uncommon and/or non-standardized shape as textually described using an associated attribute.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Is MRCC
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A statement that expresses if a Coast Guard station performs the function of a Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Snow Cover
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A description of the amount of snow covering the ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Little Snow Cover
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Little snow cover.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin Snow Cover (5 cm)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice covered with snow up to 5 cm deep.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 20 cm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Snow cover is less than 20cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Snow Cover (5 to 20 cm)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The depth of snow coverage is from 5 to 20 centimetres.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: 5 cm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Snow cover is greater than 5cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick Snow Cover (20 cm)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice covered with snow over 20 cm deep.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Snow Cover
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No snow cover.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Magnetic Anomaly Detector Signature
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indication of the strength of the Magnetic Anomaly Detector reading caused by the object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nil Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has no magnetic reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Slight Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a slight reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a moderate magnetic reading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Strong Magnetic Reading
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has a strong magnetic reading.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Weed/Kelp
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of marine vegetation of the algae class.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Kelp
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A giant plant sometimes 60 metres long with no roots, it is anchored by hold-fasts or tendrils up to 10 metres long, that cling to rock. Gas filled bubbles on fronds act as floats keeping the kelp just below the surface.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Seaweed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The general name for marine plants of the Algae class which grow in long narrow ribbons.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sargasso
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A certain type of seaweed, or more generally, a large floating mass of this seaweed.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Minehunting Classification
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the profile of the seabed for minehunting purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Smooth Minehunting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Very few craters, gullies, ridges or seaweed patches (5% of the area or less), sand ripples 150mm high or less.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Moderate Minehunting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Large numbers of craters, gullies, ridges or seaweed patches (5 to 15% of the area), sand ripples 150 to 300 mm high.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rough Minehunting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Extensive areas (over 15% of the whole) of craters etc., or large sand ripples or closely spaced sandwaves.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Very Rough Minehunting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Very extensive areas (over 50% of the whole).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Species Grouping
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The generalised group of organisms for which an area has been designated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cetacean
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of an order (Cetacea) of aquatic mostly marine mammals that includes the whales, dolphins, porpoises, and related forms and that have a torpedo-shaped nearly hairless body, paddle-shaped forelimbs but no hind limbs, one or two nares opening externally at the top of the head, and a horizontally flattened tail used for locomotion.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pinniped
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of an order or suborder (Pinnipedia) of aquatic carnivorous mammals (such as a seal or walrus) with all four limbs modified into flippers.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Vertebrate cold blooded animal with gills, living in water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Turtle
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of an order (Testudines synonym Chelonia) of terrestrial, freshwater, and marine reptiles that have a toothless horny beak and a shell of bony dermal plates usually covered with horny shields enclosing the trunk and into which the head, limbs, and tail usually may be withdrawn.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bird
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of a class (Aves) of warm-blooded vertebrates distinguished by having the body more or less completely covered with feathers and the forelimbs modified as wings.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sirenian
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of an order (Sirenia) of aquatic herbivorous mammals (such as a manatee, dugong, or Steller's sea cow) that have large forelimbs resembling paddles, no hind limbs, and a flattened tail resembling a fin.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Otter
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Plane surface towed forward of its middle length so that it will incline and dive. Used in fishing, minesweeping or surveying. See Kite, Kite Otter, and Oropesa Sweep.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Polar Bear
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large creamy-white carnivorous bear (Ursus maritimus synonym Thalarctos maritimus) that inhabits arctic regions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sea Snake
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of numerous venomous aquatic chiefly viviparous elapid snakes of warm seas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coral Reef
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A reef, often of large extent, composed chiefly of coral and its derivatives.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Controlled Airspace Class Designation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Air traffic services and rules of operation (e.g. instrument (IFR), and, visual (VFR), flight rules etc.) that are applicable to the controlled airspace, as defined by the governing aviation authority and in accordance with ICAO standards.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class A
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR flights only are permitted, all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class B
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, all flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from each other.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class C
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, all flights are provided with air traffic control service and IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and from VFR flights. VFR flights are separated from IFR flights and receive traffic information in respect of other VFR flights.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class D
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted and all flights are provided with air traffic control service, IFR flights are separated from other IFR flights and receive traffic information in respect of VFR flights, VFR flights receive traffic information in respect of all other flights.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class E
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, IFR flights are provided with air traffic control service and are separated from other IFR flights. All flights receive traffic information as far as is practical. Class E shall not be used for control zones.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class F
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted, all participating IFR flights receive an air traffic advisory service and all flights receive flight information service if requested.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Controlled Airspace Class G
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: IFR and VFR flights are permitted and receive flight information service if requested.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Cardinal Point Orientation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The angle of the major axis of the object expressed to the nearest 45 degrees using cardinal compass point notation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: north/south
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object is orientated on average along a north-south axis.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: east/west
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object is orientated on average along a east-west axis.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: northeast/southwest
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object is orientated on average along a northeast-southwest axis.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: northwest/southeast
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: the object is orientated on average along a northwest-southeast axis.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Suitability for ACV Use
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Suitability for use by Air Cushioned Vehicles.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Significant Features Detected
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A statement expressing if significant features have or have not been detected in the course of a survey.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Headline
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Words set at the head of a passage or page to introduce or categorize.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Permitted Draught
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The maximum draught of a vessel permitted along a route, in a channel or dock, at a berth, or over a submerged feature.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Undetectable Mines Ratio with Burial
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The fraction of undetectable mines due to total mine burial.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Reporting/Radio Calling-In Point
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Category of reporting/radio calling-in point.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Reporting/Radio calling in point
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The location at which vessels are required to report to a traffic control center.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Ice
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fast Ice
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which remains fast, generally in the position where originally formed, and which may attain a considerable thickness. It is found along coasts, where it is attached to the shore, or over shoals, where it may be held in position by islands, grounded icebergs or grounded polar ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Glacier
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A mass of snow and ice continuously moving from higher to lower ground or, if afloat, continuously spreading.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Polar Ice
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice that is more than one year old (in contrast to winter ice). The WMO code defines polar ice as any sea ice more than one year old and more than 3 metres thick.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Right Q-Route Width
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The right-hand channel width of a Q-Route expressed as the measurement taken from the route centreline to the channel limit when proceeding UP a Q-route (e.g. A to B to C to D).

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Building Shape
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The specific shape of the building.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: High-Rise Building
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A building having many storeys.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pyramid
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A polyhedron of which one face is a polygon of any number of sides, and the other faces are triangles with a common vertex.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cylindrical
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Shaped like a cylinder, which is a solid geometrical figure generated by straight lines fixed in direction and describing with one of its points a closed curve, especially a circle.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Spherical
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Shaped like a sphere, which is a body the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cubic
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A shape the sides of which are six equal squares; a regular hexahedron.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Pictorial Representation
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The file name of an externally referenced picture file.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Combination Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the 2nd Partial Concentration
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Describes combination(s) of Ice Stage of Development and Floe Size for the second partial concentration in an ice area. Up to three (stage of development / form of ice) combinations are allowed to describe the ice in the second partial concentration group.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pancake Ice (30 cm to 3 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Predominantly circular plates of ice from 30 cm to 3 m in diameter, and up to about 10 cm in thickness, with raised rims due to the pieces striking against one another. It may be formed on a slight swell from grease ice, shuga or slush or as a result of the breaking of ice rind, nilas or, under heavy swell, of grey ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shuga/Small Ice Cake; Brash Ice (2 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An accumulation of spongy white ice lumps, a few centimetres across; they are formed from grease ice or slush and sometimes from anchor ice rising to the surface. Accumulations of floating ice made up of fragments not more than 2 m across, the wreckage of other forms of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Cake (20 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any relatively flat piece of sea ice less than 20 m across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Small Floe (20 to 100 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, from 20 to 100 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium Floe (100 to 500 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 100 m to 500 m across. Floes are subdivided according to horizontal extent.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Big Floe (500 to 2000 m) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Separate patch of floating ice or flat sheet of unbroken pack ice, greater than 20 metres (22 yards) across. A big floe is a floe of size 500 to 2000 metres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Vast Floe (2 - 10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any contiguous piece of sea ice, 2-10 kilometres across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Giant Floe (10 km) - Floe Size (FF)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A relatively flat piece of sea ice 10 km or more across.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Stage of Development - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: No stage of development - ice stage of development (SS).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: New Ice (5 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Recently formed ice which includes frazil ice, grease ice, slush and shuga and which is of less than 5 centimetres thickness. These types of ice are composed of ice crystals which are only weakly frozen together (if at all) and have a definite form only while they are afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Nilas Ice (10 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A thin elastic crust of ice, easily bending on waves and swell and under pressure, thrusting in a pattern of interlocking 'fingers' (finger rafting). Has a matt surface and is up to 10 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into dark nilas and light nilas.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Young Ice (10 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice in the transition stage between nilas and first-year ice, 10-30 cm in thickness. May be subdivided into grey ice and grey-white ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey Ice (10 to 15 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 10-15 cm thick. Less elastic than nilas and breaks in swell. Usually rafts under pressure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey - White Ice (15 to 30 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Young ice 15-30 cm thick. Under pressure it is more likely to ridge than to raft.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: First Year Ice (30 to 200 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The ages and thicknesses of the ice. First year ice is sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 30 cm - 2 m, and sometimes slightly more.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice (30 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 1 (30 to 50 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 30-50 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thin First Year Ice Stage 2 (50 to 70 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice 50-70 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium First Year Ice (70 to 120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice of not more than one winter's growth, developing from young ice; thickness 70 cm - 120 cm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Thick First Year Ice (120 cm) - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice over 120 cm thick.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Residual Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: First-year ice that has survived the summers melt and is now in the new cycle of growth. It is 30 to 180 cm thick depending on the region where it was in summer. After 1 January (in the Southern hemisphere after 1 July), this ice is called second-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Old Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has survived at least one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 3m or more. It is subdivided into residual first-year ice, second-year ice and multi-year ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Second Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice which has survived only one summer's melt; typical thickness up to 2.5 m and sometimes more. Because it is thicker than first-year ice, it stands higher out of the water. In contrast to multi-year ice, summer melting produces a regular pattern of numerous small puddles. Bare patches and puddles usually greenish-blue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Multi-Year Ice - Ice Stage of Development (SS)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Old ice up to 3 m or more thick that has survived at least two summers' melt. Hummocks are even smoother than in second-year ice and attain a look of mounds and hills. The surface of multiyear ice fields in places not subject to deformations is also hillocky due to non-uniform multiple melting. The ice is almost salt-free. Its color, where bare, is usually blue. As a result of melting, round puddles appear at its surface in summer and a well-developed drainage system is formed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Cardinal Mark
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The four quadrants (north, east, south and west) are bounded by the true bearings NW-NE, NE-SE, SE-SW and SW-NW taken from the point of interest. A cardinal mark is named after the quadrant in which it is placed. The name of the cardinal mark indicates that it should be passed to the named side of the mark.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: North Cardinal Mark
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing NW-NE taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the north side of the mark.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: East Cardinal Mark
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing NE-SE taken from the point of interest. It should be passed to the east side of the mark.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: South Cardinal Mark
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing SE-SW taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the south side of the mark.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: West Cardinal Mark
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Quadrant bounded by the true bearing SW-NW taken from the point of interest; it should be passed to the west side of the mark.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Sector Line Length
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A sector is the part of a circle between two straight lines drawn from the centre to the circumference. Sector line length specifies the displayed length of the line, in ground units, defining the limit of the sector.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Species
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A group of individuals having common characteristics, specialised from others of the same genus

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Line Spacing Minimum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The minimum distance between hydrographic survey lines.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Restriction
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The official legal statute of each kind of restricted area.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Anchoring Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which anchoring is not permitted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Anchoring Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which anchoring is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fishing Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which fishing is not permitted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fishing Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which fishing is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Trawling Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which trawling is not permitted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Trawling Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which trawling is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Entry Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: [1] An area shown on charts within which navigation and/or anchoring is prohibited. [2] In aviation terminology, a specified area within the land areas of a state or territorial waters adjacent thereto over which the flight of aircraft is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Entry Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which navigation is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dredging Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which dredging is not permitted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dredging Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which dredging is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Diving Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which diving is not permitted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Diving Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by appropriate authority, within which diving is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Wake
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Mariners must adjust the speed of their vessels to reduce the wave or wash which may cause erosion or disturb moored vessels.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Area To Be Avoided
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An IMO declared routeing measure comprising an area within defined limits in which either navigation is particularly hazardous or it is exceptionally important to avoid casualties and which should be avoided by all ships, or certain classes of ships.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Construction Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The erection of permanent or temporary fixed structures or artificial islands is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Discharging Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which discharging or dumping is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Discharging Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by an appropriate authority, within which discharging or dumping is restricted in accordance with specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Industrial or Mineral Exploration/Development Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which industrial or mineral exploration and development are prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Industrial or Mineral Exploration/Development Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by an appropriate authority, within which industrial or mineral exploration and development is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Drilling Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which excavating a hole on the seabed with a drill is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Drilling Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A specified area designated by an appropriate authority, within which excavating a hole on the seabed with a drill is restricted in accordance with certain specified conditions.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Removal of Historical Artefacts Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which the removal of historical artefacts is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cargo Transhipment (Lightening) Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which cargo transhipment (lightening) is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dragging Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which the dragging of anything along the seabed, for example bottom trawling, is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stopping Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which a vessel is prohibited from stopping.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Landing Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which landing is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Speed Restricted
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which speed is restricted.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Swimming Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area in which swimming is prohibited.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Power-Driven Vessels Prohibited
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area within which any vessel propelled by machinery is prohibited.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Burial Mechanism
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The method by which an object has or could become buried.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Liquefaction
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has become buried by the process whereby under certain conditions, a solid seafloor sediment behaves as a liquid.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sandwave Migration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has become buried by the movement of sandwaves.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sediment Migration
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has become buried by the movement of sediment.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Nature of Surface
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The general material which the land surface or the seabed is composed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mud
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Soft, wet earth.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Clay
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: (Particles of less than 0.002mm); stiff, sticky earth that becomes hard when baked.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Silt
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An unconsolidated sediment whose particles range in size from 0.0039 to 0.0625 millimetres in diameter (between clay and sand size).

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sand
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Loose material consisting of small but easily distinguishable, separate grains, between 0.0625 and 2.000 millimetres in diameter.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stone
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A general term for rock and rock fragments ranging in size from pebbles and gravel to boulders or large rock masses.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Gravel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: (Particles of 2.0 - 4.0mm); small stones with coarse sand.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pebbles
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A small stone worn smooth and rounded by the action of water, sand, ice, etc. ranging in diameter between 4 and 64 millimetres.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cobbles
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A naturally rounded stone larger than a pebble.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rock
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any formation of natural origin that constitutes an integral part of the lithosphere. The natural occurring material that forms firm, hard, and solid masses.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lava
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The fluid or semi-fluid matter flowing from a volcano. The substance that results from the cooling of the molten rock. Part of the ocean bed is composed of lava.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coral
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Hard calcareous skeletons of many tribes of marine polyps.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Shells
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The hard outside covering of an animal. Part of the ocean bed is composed of numerous shells of marine animals.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Boulder
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rounded rock with diameter of 256 millimetres or larger.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Slope
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of a stretch of ground forming a natural or artificial incline.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cutting
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An excavation through high ground for a road, canal, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Embankment
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A man-made raised long mound of earth or other material.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Cliff
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Land rising abruptly for a considerable distance above the water or surrounding land.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Frequency of Leads or Fractures
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the frequency of leads or fractures in number per nautical mile.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: layerNumber
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Number of geological layer, ascending from the lowest identified layer.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Status of Small Bottom Object
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Current minehunting status of the object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Detected (MILEC)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Minelike echoes have been selected from within the sonar clutter.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Classified (MILCO)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been classified as a minelike object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Classified (NON-MILCO)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been classified as a non-minelike object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Identified (NOMBO)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been positively identified as a non mine minelike bottom object.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Identified (Mine)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been positively identified as a mine.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Identified (UXO)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been positively identified as an Unexploded Ordnance.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Countermined
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The mine has been exploded by an explosive charge placed close to the mine.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Neutralised
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The mine has been rendered incapable of firing though may still remain dangerous to handle.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Removed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The mine has been taken out of an area where its detonation would be unacceptable.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Swept
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The object has been removed or destroyed by minesweepers using explosive or mechanical gear.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Clearance Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The physical horizontal clearance distance between two points on a feature, such as a bridge span, dock, gate, lock or tunnel.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Nature of Surface - Qualifying Terms
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The nature of various forms of natural surface materials in terms of their size, morphology and consistency.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fine
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Falls within the smallest size continuum for a particular nature of surface term.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Medium
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Falls within the moderate size continuum for a particular nature of surface term.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Coarse
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Falls within the largest size continuum for a particular nature of surface term.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Broken
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Fractured or in pieces.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sticky
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an adhesive or glue like property.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Soft
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Not hard or firm.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Stiff
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Not pliant; thick, resistant to flow.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Volcanic
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Composed of or containing material ejected from a volcano.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Calcareous
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Composed of or containing calcium or calcium carbonate.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Hard
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Firm; usually refers to an area of the seafloor not covered by unconsolidated sediment.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Marine Farm/Culture
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of an area of water devoted to the raising, breeding, or production of a specific aquatic animal.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Crustaceans
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Hard shelled animals, for example crabs or lobsters.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Edible Bivalve Molluscs
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A two-part hinged external shell covering that contains a soft-bodied invertebrate.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fish
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Vertebrate cold blooded animal with gills, living in water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Seaweed
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The general name for marine plants of the Algae class which grow in long narrow ribbons.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pearl Culture Farm
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area where pearls are artificially cultivated.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Opening Bridge
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of opening structures spanning and providing passage over a gap or barrier, such as a river or roadway.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Swing Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A movable bridge (or span thereof) which rotates in a horizontal plane about a vertical pivot to allow the passage of vessels.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Lifting Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A movable bridge (or span thereof) which is capable of being lifted vertically to allow vessels to pass beneath.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bascule Bridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A counterpoise bridge rotated in a vertical plane about an axis at one or both ends.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Drawbridge
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A general name for bridges of which part or the entire span of the bridge may be raised or drawn aside to allow ships to pass through.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Speed Minimum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Rate of motion. The terms speed and velocity are often used interchangeably, but speed is a scalar, having magnitude only, while velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction. Speed minimum is the minimum rate of travel that can occur.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Maximum Altitude
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Height (AGL - above ground level) above surface level to the highest portion of the feature.

S100FC:uom.S100Base:name: foot
S100FC:uom.S100Base:definition: a unit of length equal to 12 inches, 1/6 of a fathom, or 30.480 centimetres

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Scale Minimum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The minimum scale at which the feature may be used for example for ECDIS presentation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Signal Group
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The number of signals, the combination of signals or the morse character(s) within one period of full sequence.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Default Clearance Depth
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The depth value determined for an underwater hazard of unknown depth, based on the depth of the surrounding area.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Wreck
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of a wrecked or ruined ship.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Non-Dangerous Wreck
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A wreck which is not considered to be dangerous to surface navigation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dangerous Wreck
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A wreck submerged at such a depth as to be considered dangerous to surface navigation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Distributed Remains of Wreck
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A substantively decayed wreck over which it is safe to navigate but which should be avoided for anchoring, taking the ground or ground fishing.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wreck Showing Mast/Masts
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Wreck of which only the mast(s) is visible at the sounding datum indicated.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Wreck Showing Any Portion of Hull or Superstructure
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Wreck of which any portion of the hull or superstructure is visible at the sounding datum indicated.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Depth Range Minimum Value
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The minimum (shoalest) value of a depth range.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Pylon
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of the pylon based on the service it is supporting.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Power Transmission Pylon/Pole
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pylon or pole that supports one or more power lines.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Telephone/Telegraph Pylon/Pole
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pylon or pole that supports one or more communication lines.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Aerial Cableway Pylon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tower or pylon supporting steel cables which convey cars, buckets, or other suspended carrier units.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bridge Pylon/Tower
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tower and/or pylon from which the deck of a bridge is suspended.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Bridge Pier
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A pillar or abutment that supports a bridge span.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pipeline Pylon
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A tower or pylon supporting a suspended pipeline or pipelines.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Date Start
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The earliest date on which an object (for example a buoy) will be present.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Dredged Date
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The date that dredging occurred.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Coastline
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Physical condition of the coastline.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Steep Coast
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A coast backed by rock or earth cliffs, gives a good radar return and is useful for visual identification from a considerable distance off, where cliffs alternate with low lying coast along the shoreline.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flat Coast
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A level coast with no obvious topographic features.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Glacier, Seaward End
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Projecting seaward extension of glacier, usually afloat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mangrove
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: One of several genera of tropical trees or shrubs which produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying coasts into shallow water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Marshy Shore
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A shoreline area made up of spongy land saturated with water. It may have a shallow covering of water, usually with a considerable amount of vegetation appearing above the surface.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Ice Coast
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A vertical cliff forming the seaward edge of an ice shelf, ranging in height from 2 metres to 50 metres or more above sea level.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: In Dispute
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: A statement that expresses if an area is in a jurisdictional dispute.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Bottom Feature Classification
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of naturally occurring bottom features on the seabed.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Fault
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: In geology, a break of shear in the earth's crust with an observable displacement between the two sides of the break, and parallel to the plane of the break.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Sandwave
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A large mobile wave-like sediment feature in shallow water and composed of sand. The wavelength may reach 100 metres, the amplitude may be up to 20 metres.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Category of Offshore Platform
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Classification of an offshore raised structure.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Oil Rig
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A temporary mobile structure, either fixed or floating, used in the exploration stages of oil and gas fields.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Production Platform
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A term used to indicate a permanent offshore structure equipped to control the flow of oil or gas. It does not include entirely submarine structures.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Observation/Research Platform
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A platform from which one's surroundings or events can be observed, noted or recorded such as for scientific study.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Articulated Loading Platform
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A metal lattice tower, buoyant at one end and attached at the other by a universal joint to a concrete filled base on the seabed. The platform may be fitted with a helicopter platform, emergency accommodation and hawser/hose retrieval.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Single Anchor Leg Mooring
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A rigid frame or tube with a buoyancy device at its upper end, secured at its lower end to a universal joint on a large steel or concrete base resting on the seabed, and at its upper end to a mooring buoy by a chain or wire.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Mooring Tower
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A platform secured to the seabed and surmounted by a turntable to which ships moor.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Artificial Island
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A man-made structure usually built for the exploration or exploitation of marine resources, marine scientific research, tidal observations, etc.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Floating Production, Storage and Off-Loading Vessel
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An offshore facility consisting of a moored tanker/barge by which the product is extracted, stored and exported.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Accommodation Platform
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A platform used primarily for eating, sleeping and recreation purposes.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Navigation, Communication and Control Buoy
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A floating structure with control room, power and storage facilities, attached to the seabed by a flexible pipeline and cables.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Floating Oil Tank
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A floating structure, anchored to the seabed, for storing oil.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Measurement Distance Minimum
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The minimum spacing of the principal measurement lines of a hydrographic survey.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Colour
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The property possessed by an object of producing different sensations on the eye as a result of the way it reflects or emits light.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: White
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The achromatic object colour of greatest lightness characteristically perceived to belong to objects that reflect diffusely nearly all incident energy throughout the visible spectrum.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Black
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: The achromatic color of least lightness characteristically perceived to belong to objects that neither reflect nor transmit light.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Red
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A color whose hue resembles that of blood or of the ruby or is that of the long-wave extreme of the visible spectrum.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Green
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Of the color green.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Blue
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A color whose hue is that of the clear sky or that of the portion of the color spectrum lying between green and violet.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Yellow
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A color whose hue resembles that of ripe lemons or sunflowers or is that of the portion of the spectrum lying between green and orange.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Grey
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Of the color grey.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Brown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of a group of colors between red and yellow in hue, of medium to low lightness, and of moderate to low saturation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Amber
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A variable color averaging a dark orange yellow.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Violet
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of a group of colors of reddish-blue hue, low lightness, and medium saturation.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Orange
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of a group of colors that are between red and yellow in hue.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Magenta
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: A deep purplish red.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Pink
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any of a group of colors bluish red to red in hue, of medium to high lightness, and of low to moderate saturation.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Horizontal Distance Uncertainty
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The best estimate of the horizontal accuracy of horizontal clearances and distances.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Estimated Range of Transmission
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The estimated range of a non-optical electromagnetic transmission.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Undetectable Mines Ratio without Burial
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The fraction of undetectable mines and masked mines caused by the bottom profile and the clutter density.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Melt Stage
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: The different stages at which water becomes altered from a solid to a liquid state, usually by heat.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Few Puddles
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 1/10 - 3/10 coverage of puddles. A puddle is an accumulation of water on ice, mainly due to the melting of snow, but in some more advanced stages also the melting of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Many Puddles
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area of numerous accumulation of water on ice, mainly due to the melting of snow, but in some more advanced stages also the melting of ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Flooded Ice
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice, usually first-year ice, flooded by a melt or river water layer.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Few Thaw Holes
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 1/10 - 3/10 coverage of thaw holes. A thaw hole is a vertical hole formed in ice when surface puddles melt through to the underlying water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Many Thaw Holes
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: An area of numerous vertical holes in sea ice formed when surface puddles melt through to the underlying water.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Dried Ice
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Ice surface from which water has disappeared after the formation of cracks and thaw holes. During the process of drying the surface whitens.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Rotten Ice
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Sea ice which has become honey-combed (laced) and is in an advanced state of disintegration.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Few Frozen Puddles
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: 1/10 - 3/10 coverage of frozen puddles. A frozen puddle is an accumulation of water on ice, mainly due to the melting of snow, but in some more advanced stages also the melting of ice, that has frozen over.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: All Puddles Frozen
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: All puddles frozen.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: No Melt
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Absence of puddles, flooded ice, thaw hole, dried ice and rotten ice.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Undetermined/Unknown
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Having an unknown value.

S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:name: Ice Fracture Type
S100FC:S100_FC_SimpleAttribute.S100FC:definition: Indicates the type of ice fracture, based upon width.

S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:label: Crack (0 to 1 m Wide)
S100FC:listedValue.S100FC:definition: Any fracture or rift in floating ice (0 to 1 metre wide) not sufficiently wide to be described as a lead.
